$comment: THE SIX LEGAL DECISIONS N-PARTY SUPPORT CANNOT MAKE FOR ITSELF.
Invariant 60 reduced 23 binary clauses to six shapes, of which four generalise without
anybody choosing anything. These are the other two, and the six clauses that carry them.
EVERY DECISION HERE IS `UNDECIDED`, AND THAT IS A RESULT, NOT A PLACEHOLDER. The engine
must not select a legal interpretation by default. A document with three parties and an
unresolved apportionment must say the point is open rather than quietly adopt one reading —
which is the same discipline the requirement layer already applies with UNRESOLVED and
THE COUNTERFACTUALS ARE THE POINT. Each decision shows its consequence at two, three and
four parties. At two, the candidate treatments produce identical words, which is exactly why
the ambiguity survived this long unnoticed. At three they diverge, and for the liability cap
Candidate treatments are named so an advocate has something to choose between. Naming them
is not proposing them, and the order they appear in is not a recommendation.

decisions.binary_text: the aggregate liability of either Party under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid or payable under this Agreement
decisions.legal_question: Where there are more than two parties, is the cap a separate ceiling for each party, one ceiling shared between them all, or a limit that operates only between the parties and leaves third-party exposure untouched?

authority_basis.note: Compensation for loss caused by breach — what the cap limits.
A sum named in the contract is recoverable as reasonable compensation, not automatically in full.
Every partner is liable jointly with all the others and severally to third parties. A cap agreed between partners cannot bind someone who is not a party to it.

candidate_treatments.reading: Each party has its own ceiling of X.
One ceiling of X across all parties together.
The ceiling governs claims between the parties and does not limit what a third party may recover.

decisions.why_the_two_party_document_hides_it: At two parties PER_PARTY and INTER_SE_ONLY produce the same words and the same arithmetic against each other; only a third-party claim separates them, and the instrument never mentions one. SHARED differs even at two but the difference is invisible without a second concurrent claim.

decisions.binary_text: Each Party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other Party and its directors, officers, employees, and authorised representatives
decisions.legal_question: Where there are more than two parties, does each party indemnify each other party severally for the whole loss, or do the indemnifying parties share one liability between them?

authority_basis.note: Contract of indemnity — one party promises to save the other from loss.
The indemnity-holder's rights, which is where the quantum of a multi-party indemnity actually bites.

candidate_treatments.reading: Every party indemnifies every other party in full.
The indemnifying parties are liable together and individually for the whole.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: claimant may recover the whole from any one of the other two
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: claimant may recover the whole from any one of the other three

candidate_treatments.reading: Each indemnifier is liable for its share, measured by contribution or profit ratio.
candidate_treatments.consequence_2: shares must be stated or implied
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: requires a share per party — which the instrument does not currently carry
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: same, and the shares must still total the whole

decisions.why_the_two_party_document_hides_it: With one indemnifier and one indemnitee, several, joint-and-several and proportionate all mean the same thing: that one party pays. The distinction only exists once there is more than one person who might be asked.

decisions.binary_text: by either Party with immediate effect if the other Party commits a material breach of this Agreement and fails to cure it
decisions.legal_question: Where there are more than two parties, does the innocent party end the whole instrument, or only its own relationship with the defaulting party, leaving the instrument on foot between the rest?

authority_basis.note: Where a party refuses or disables itself from performing, the promisee may put an end to the contract.
Dissolution of a firm — the dissolution of the partnership between ALL the partners.
Expulsion of a partner, which is the other thing this right might mean and is subject to express agreement and good faith.

candidate_treatments.reading: One default terminates the agreement as to everybody.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: two innocent parties lose the arrangement because of a third's default

candidate_treatments.reading: The defaulter ceases to be a party; the instrument continues between the others.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: the firm continues between the remaining two — expulsion, not dissolution

candidate_treatments.reading: The right is exercisable only by the innocent parties acting together.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: one innocent party alone cannot terminate

decisions.why_the_two_party_document_hides_it: With two parties, ending the relationship and ending the instrument are the same act, and there is no such thing as 'the remaining parties'. All three treatments collapse into one sentence. For a partnership the difference is dissolution under s.39 versus expulsion under s.33, which are not close.

decisions.binary_text: the exiting Party shall provide the other Party with reasonable assistance
decisions.legal_question: Where there are more than two parties, is the exiting party's assistance owed to each remaining party separately, to them collectively, or to the continuing entity?

authority_basis.note: The obligation of parties to perform, which survives to the extent the contract provides.

candidate_treatments.reading: Assistance owed separately to every remaining party.
Assistance owed to the firm or venture rather than to its members.
candidate_treatments.consequence_2: no entity distinct from the counterparty

decisions.why_the_two_party_document_hides_it: With two parties there is no continuing entity distinct from the remaining party, so the two treatments name the same recipient.

decisions.binary_text: Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be attempted to be resolved amicably between the Parties. If the dispute remains unresolved within fifteen (15) days of written notice, it shall be referred to arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
decisions.legal_question: Where there are more than two parties, may one party refer a dispute against one other party alone and leave the rest out, or must every party be joined to a single arbitration?

authority_basis.note: An arbitration agreement is an agreement to submit to arbitration disputes between the parties to it. Where three parties sign one agreement, all three are parties to the arbitration agreement — which is what makes the scope question live rather than academic.

Where the parties fail to agree on a sole arbitrator, the appointment is made by the arbitral institution designated under Section 11(3A). This fallback is count-independent and is the reason the APPOINTMENT half of this clause needs no decision.

The parties shall be treated with equality. This is why 'jointly appointed by the Parties' must mean all of them, and why a clause giving each side its own nominee arbitrator would raise a problem this clause does not — it specifies a sole arbitrator.
An arbitral award is final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them. A party who was never joined is neither, so a bilateral award settles nothing as against the third.
Res judicata. A third party not bound by the award is free to litigate the same facts, which is where the inconsistent-outcome exposure actually lands.

statutory_gap: THE ACT DOES NOT ANSWER THIS. The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 as amended through 2021 contains no
provision for joinder of parties or consolidation of arbitral proceedings. The Supreme Court permitted
consolidation in PR Shah v B.H.H. Securities and the Delhi High Court in Gammon India v NHAI, but as judicial
practice rather than as an entitlement a party can insist on, and an ad hoc reference has no institutional
rules to fall back on. The draft Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2024 does not address it and
So the instrument is the only place this could have been settled, and it does not settle it. That is what
makes this UNDECIDED rather than merely unstated: there is no default to fall back on.

candidate_treatments.reading: A party may refer its dispute against one other party alone; the others are not joined.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: an award between two of three binds neither the third nor anyone claiming under them, and the third may litigate the same facts to a different result on the same instrument
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: same, with three strangers to each award and correspondingly more ways for the instrument to be construed two ways at once

candidate_treatments.reading: Any reference must join every party to the instrument.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: one award binds all three and inconsistency is impossible, at the cost of dragging an uninvolved party into every dispute and its costs
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: same, and the cost of the uninvolved grows with each party

candidate_treatments.reading: A reference may begin bilaterally, and any other party may elect to be joined, or be joined on the application of a party, before the tribunal is constituted.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: the third chooses whether to be bound, which requires the clause to state a joinder window and who decides — none of which the current text contains
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: same, and the window has to accommodate several electing parties

decisions.why_the_two_party_document_hides_it: With two parties, referring 'the dispute' and referring it 'against the other party' are the same act, and there is no such person as a party who might be left out. All three treatments collapse into one sentence. The clause is not ambiguous at two parties — it is complete, and it stops being complete the moment a third signature appears.

settled.why: A good-faith discussion among three is the same obligation as between two; no right is gained or lost by either reading.

All principals must agree, and on failure Section 11(5) appoints regardless of how many there are. Because the clause specifies a SOLE arbitrator, the multi-party appointment problem — three parties unable each to have a nominee without unequal treatment under Section 18 — does not arise.
'Nothing in this clause prevents a Party from applying to a competent court' is distributive already.

open.why: Bilateral or multilateral, with no statutory default.

decisions.binary_text: Expiry or termination of this Agreement shall not affect any right, remedy, obligation, or liability of a Party that has accrued as at the date of expiry or termination... the provisions of this Agreement relating to confidentiality, ownership of intellectual property, indemnity, limitation of liability, dispute resolution, governing law and jurisdiction, notices, and this clause shall survive expiry or termination and shall continue to bind the Parties.
decisions.legal_question: Where one party ceases to be a party but the instrument continues between the others, does the departing party remain bound by the provisions expressed to survive — given that the clause's trigger is expiry or termination of THIS AGREEMENT, which has not occurred, and its survivors bind THE PARTIES, of whom the departing party is no longer one?

note: THIS QUESTION DOES NOT ALWAYS EXIST. Under ENDS_THE_INSTRUMENT and under
REQUIRES_ALL_INNOCENT_PARTIES the trigger fires, every former party stays bound by the
survivors, and there is nothing further to decide. It arises under exactly ONE of the three
So it is neither merely inherited nor independent, and recording it as either would be wrong:
inherited would assert a question under treatments where none exists; independent would hide
that choosing ENDS_THE_INSTRUMENT disposes of it entirely.

counterfactual_evidence.method: Enumerate, for every pair of three principals, which regime binds them after Party 1's default.
the_gap: Under World B the pairs involving the departing party fall outside BOTH regimes. The LIVE
regime does not reach them because Party 1 is no longer a Party; the SURVIVING regime does
not reach them because 'this Agreement' has not expired or terminated — it is on foot
The departing party therefore walks away from confidentiality and intellectual-property
obligations, not because anyone released them but because the trigger is a global predicate
and the termination was partial. The gap does not exist at two parties, where partial
termination is not a thing that can happen.

authority_basis.note: Parties must perform or offer to perform their promises unless dispensed with under the Act. A party who ceases to be a party is not thereby dispensed with as to what has already accrued.
Where a party refuses or disables itself from performing, the promisee may put an end to the contract — the provision that makes partial termination arguable at all.
Expulsion of a partner. The firm continues; the expelled partner's continuing duties are governed by the contract between the partners, which is precisely what this clause fails to state for them.

After dissolution, a partner may restrain the others from using the firm property or name — an example of an obligation the statute continues expressly, which this instrument does not do for a departing party.
Relevant to the confidentiality survivor: a restraint on a departing party must still be a lawful restraint, so 'they remain bound' is not automatically the safe answer.

candidate_treatments.reading: The survivors bind a departing party as if the instrument had terminated as to them.
candidate_treatments.consequence_2: indistinguishable — with two parties, one leaving IS termination
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: confidentiality and IP obligations follow the departing party out; the instrument continues unchanged between the remaining two

candidate_treatments.reading: Only accrued rights survive against them; forward-looking survivors do not.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: the departing party may use confidential information from the date of departure, and the remaining parties have no contractual remedy
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: same, and the exposure compounds with each departure

candidate_treatments.reading: The instrument is treated as terminated as to the departing party alone, so the clause operates for their pairs and the instrument continues for the rest.
candidate_treatments.consequence_3: requires the clause to say what 'termination of this Agreement' means when termination is partial — wording the instrument does not currently contain
candidate_treatments.consequence_4: same, and the drafting must handle several partial terminations at different dates

decisions.why_the_two_party_document_hides_it: With two parties there is no such event as one party ceasing to be a party while the instrument continues. Departure and termination are the same act, the trigger always fires, and all three treatments produce identical words. The gap is not latent in the two-party deed; it does not exist there.
compounding: Three of the nine enumerated survivors carry open decisions of their own: indemnity
resolution (ARBITRATION_REFERENCE_SCOPE). Under World B the departing party escapes the cap
as well — which cuts both ways, because the cap that no longer binds them no longer protects
them either. Whether that is a windfall or an exposure depends on the apportionment question
that is itself open, so these decisions cannot sensibly be taken in isolation.

note: Six decisions over eight clauses. SURVIVAL_AGAINST_A_DEPARTING_PARTY is the first CONDITIONAL
decision in this file: it carries `conditional_on`, because it arises under exactly one of the
three treatments of its parent and does not exist under the other two.
That structure matters for how the backlog is counted. An advocate who chooses ENDS_THE_INSTRUMENT
closes two questions at once; an advocate who chooses ENDS_THAT_RELATIONSHIP opens a second one.
A flat list of open decisions would show neither.
Until each is authored, a document with more than two parties must report the point as open rather
